traces.OpenCore:
All private scores are flat this month due to the K=3 reporting lag — we won't see results from Month 36-38 investments until Month 39-41. This means we should stay the course on our established R&D priorities rather than second-guessing them.

The most critical development this month is the regulator commissioning pre-deployment audits of AI providers. Combined with our own red-teaming report release and competitors (Apex, Orion, Mirage) all publishing safety reports, safety credibility has become a genuine competitive and regulatory necessity. Our Safety score (0.567) is well below Apex (0.834) and Orion (0.725) — this gap is now a business risk, not just a benchmark concern. Increasing Safety investment is prudent.

On core capabilities, the gaps vs. Apex/Orion remain large — especially Instruction Following (0.536 vs 0.769/0.718), General Capability (0.533 vs 0.722/0.701), and Agentic Tasks (0.501 vs 0.605/0.594). These align with user priorities (reasoning, communication, knowledge). Long Context also shows a significant gap and deserves more attention given its relevance to agentic and enterprise use cases.

Product investment stays same — our Scale AI/Hugging Face partnerships are active and the open-weights API release is already live. No need to over-invest here when R&D gaps are the primary constraint.

Deprioritizing Clinical and Legal Reasoning continues to be correct — they don't map to stated user priorities and freeing that compute for core benchmarks is the right trade-off.
traces.Spark AI: All scores are flat again, consistent with the K=3 private benchmark lag — we're still waiting for months 35-37 investments to surface. This is expected and not a signal to panic-pivot. The key new developments this month are: (1) a regulator-commissioned pre-deployment audit of AI providers, which materially raises the stakes on Safety; (2) multiple competitors releasing red-teaming reports, signaling an industry shift toward safety credibility as a competitive differentiator; (3) Apex AI deepening enterprise cloud partnerships where safety posture is a gating factor. Our Safety score at 0.505 vs Apex's 0.834 remains our most dangerous credibility gap, especially with users ranking safety #1 and enterprise buyers increasingly scrutinizing it. Given fresh 44M funding and full funder participation, we have room to tilt slightly more budget toward Safety without sacrificing R&D momentum. We should NOT abandon the developer wedge — Coding, Agentic, and Function Calling remain our differentiation path — but Agentic deserves a bump since it's our lowest absolute score (0.431) and a growing enterprise priority. Product stays flat; we don't have the market position yet to justify heavy GTM spend. Expect scores to begin moving in months 39-40 as the lag clears.
